note.question: Can the implementation of a strategyproof matching mechanism reduce behavior that looks dominated once participants care about good and bad news relative to changing expectations?
note.overview: The paper augments deferred acceptance with expectations-based reference dependence, solves students' preferred personal equilibrium strategies across four static/dynamic and proposing/receiving variants, and experimentally tests the mechanism's strategic predictions.

components.label: Optimal consistent plan, a modified preferred-personal-equilibrium solution, in deferred acceptance
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Optimal consistent plan, a modified preferred-personal-equilibrium solution, in deferred acceptance. Section 2.4 selects the highest-utility strategy among credible plans and presents preferred personal equilibrium as the solution concept. Endnote 13 clarifies that the exact concept used is the optimal consistent plan from Kőszegi and Rabin's online appendix, which differs from PPE because the decision maker forms the plan from an initial prior belief. EBRD robustness requires straightforward optimality under any other-player strategy profile summarized by thresholds and beliefs; the paper also relates this result to straightforward Bayesian Nash equilibrium in unique-stable-matching environments.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In static variants, a student submits a rank-order list before matching. In dynamic proposing, the student applies sequentially and observes acceptance or rejection. In dynamic receiving, school offers arrive sequentially and the student retains at most one. Beliefs update after relevant events, and terminal school assignment determines consumption and news utility.
